description: The fen's other cat, and it does not hide. It walks into the firelight, looks at every face in turn, and goes.
lore: It is nothing like [[monsters/swamp_cat|the stalker]]. Squat, heavy through the shoulder, blunt in the face, and with no interest at all in cover. It comes to a fen fire, sits down inside the light where everyone can see it, and looks at the people. One at a time. It takes as long as it takes. Then it gets up and goes back out into the dark.

Hunters tell the stare as an attack, which is what people do about anything that will not stop looking at them, and the fen has a whole vocabulary for what those eyes are supposed to do to you. Watch it happen twice and the story goes flat. It is not doing anything to you. It is checking. Face, then the next face, losing interest at each one, and it has been working through faces for longer than anyone at that fire has been dead.

[[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] sits still for it. He is the one man on that circuit who has been looked over by something worse, and he will not say a word about that, but he will say this: you let it finish. Turning your face away from a thing that is looking for somebody is a rudeness he is not willing to commit. The others follow his lead now, so the fire goes quiet for a minute when the cat comes in, twelve people holding their chins up to be inspected by an animal, and then it leaves and they carry on.
gm_notes: Replaces the shipped description, and only because the shipped line and Bogstalker's were both eyes-in-the-swamp, which buried the fact that these are two species. Method is the difference: that one hides, this one walks in. The horror line is the rumour and the record quietly demotes it — it is a cat looking for its person, checking every face and losing. Hearn's courtesy is the scene; it also characterises him without touching the cave.
